name: Belle and Sebastian
label: Matador
lede: Stuart Murdoch spent seven years too ill to work, then found his songs on a Glasgow course for unemployed musicians. The band that grew around him beat Steps at the Brits, lost a singer mid-tour and, in 2017, left its drummer at a Walmart.

eras.title: A course for the unemployed
eras.text: Stuart Murdoch spent seven years too ill to work, then found his songs on a Glasgow course for unemployed musicians. A college label that had planned a single gave him an album, and a second followed within six months.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stuart Murdoch (musician) · Wikipedia: Stuart David · Wikipedia: If You're Feeling Sinister
years.h: Two Stuarts meet on a course for unemployed musicians
years.p: Murdoch, just out of years of ME/chronic fatigue syndrome, meets bassist [[Stuart David|2854838c-9119-4d95-9a44-394d05481bf5]] on Beatbox, a Stow College programme in Glasgow.
years.xp:
Murdoch was diagnosed with ME/CFS in the late 1980s and couldn't work for seven years. By early 1995 he had largely recovered. He and David first played together in bands called Lisa Helps the Blind and Rhode Island.

Murdoch lived above, and worked as caretaker for, the church hall at Hyndland Parish Church until 2003. The band rehearsed in the hall.

years.h: A student label meant to press one single, and offers an album
years.p: The Stow College music business course, led by former Associates member Alan Rankine, likes the demos enough to let Murdoch make a full record on its student-run Electric Honey label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belle and Sebastian · Wikipedia: Isobel Campbell · Wikipedia: Tigermilk
years.h: A band gets recruited at the Grosvenor Café
years.p: Murdoch and David sign up [[Stevie Jackson|32afcb9a-787b-44ed-b5db-c6ea8ffb5ab1]], [[Isobel Campbell|d51f3a15-12a2-41a0-acfa-33b5eae71164]], [[Chris Geddes|6cd0aebf-b60e-46a3-8052-9976d9900127]] and David's flatmate [[Richard Colburn|e7528aba-c5e2-4917-9a52-9b61d56f9a13]]. The name comes from a Murdoch story based on the 1965 TV series about a boy and his Pyrenean mountain dog, Belle.
years.xp: Campbell was nineteen when she met Murdoch at a New Year's Eve party. Colburn was a student on the Stow College music business course.

years.cap: The Tigermilk sleeve, 1996: Joanne Kenney, photographed by Murdoch
years.h: Tigermilk sells out its 1,000 copies within months
years.p: Cut mostly live at CaVa in Glasgow, March 4 to 6, 1996, and pressed by Electric Honey. By 1999 an original was worth $600.
years.xp:
John Peel and Mark Radcliffe played it on BBC radio, which led to a session and a record deal. Murdoch took the cover photo of his then-girlfriend Joanne Kenney; the toy in the picture was auctioned for charity in 2019.

Jeepster reissued it properly in 1999, and it has since sold more than 124,000 copies.

years.h: Jeepster Records signs the band off the back of Tigermilk
years.p: The London label gets Belle and Sebastian, and violinist [[Sarah Martin|b97377be-453d-4a1b-b40e-72cff3cfefd4]] joins just before the next sessions.

years.h: Pitchfork gives If You're Feeling Sinister a 10/10
years.p: Recorded at CaVa with Tony Doogan in five days and mixed in three. Murdoch shot the cover of his friend Ciara MacLaverty, who also had chronic fatigue syndrome.
years.xp:
Martin compared making Tigermilk and Sinister back to back to the Beatles cutting Rubber Soul and Revolver. Spin later named it one of the 100 greatest albums of 1985 to 2005, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 14 of the 1990s.

Matador released it in the US in 1997.
play: The Stars of Track and Field

eras.title: The band that wouldn't pose
eras.text: Belle and Sebastian barely toured, rarely spoke to the press and sent friends to stand in for photos. Three EPs climbed the UK chart anyway, and Matador Records took them to America.

years.h: Friends stand in for the band on the sleeves
years.p: While Murdoch recovers his health, the band plays rarely, skips the press and refuses publicity photos, often asking friends to pose in its place.
years.xp: The low profile ran alongside Murdoch's ME/CFS. The band gave few interviews, and the missing faces became part of the appeal.

years.h: Dog on Wheels reaches No. 59
years.p: The first EP features Murdoch, David and trumpeter [[Mick Cooke|b6291b68-d71b-4dae-99c8-0e279dff82b5]], who won't officially join for another year.

years.h: The church where Murdoch lives doubles as a studio
years.p: Lazy Line Painter Jane is cut there, with [[Monica Queen|9a86679d-7661-4633-b1b0-76a69922458c]] singing, and reaches No. 41.

years.h: NME and Melody Maker both pick 3.. 6.. 9 Seconds of Light
years.p: Each names the EP Single of the Week. It reaches No. 32, the band's first top-40 entry.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boy with the Arab Strap
years.h: The Boy with the Arab Strap reaches UK No. 12
years.p: Jeepster releases it in Britain and Matador in America. More members write and sing: Jackson leads two songs, Campbell one, and David speaks one.
years.xp:
Cooke joins as a full member. The album sold 200,000 copies through 2006.

Pitchfork gave it 0.8 out of 10, calling it a parody of the earlier albums, then pulled that review and re-scored it 8.5 in 2018.
play: The Boy with the Arab Strap
The Boy with the Arab Strap

years.big: "There's a limit to putting someone else's name on an album."
years.h: Falkirk's Arab Strap are not amused by the title
years.p: Malcolm Middleton of the duo [[Arab Strap|6caf09f5-2f01-4f76-bcc7-6207930c56c6]], who had toured with the band, on Murdoch borrowing their name. Murdoch didn't know it was also a sex aid.

eras.title: A Brit Award, and the band splits in two
eras.text: A win over Steps at the Brits put them in the papers and on Top of the Pops. Then the founding bassist left to write novels, the cellist walked out mid-tour, and the band left Jeepster.

years.src: Wikipedia: Brit Awards 1999 · Wikipedia: Belle and Sebastian
years.h: Belle and Sebastian beat Steps at the Brits
years.p: At the London Arena they win Best British Breakthrough on the Radio 1 listener vote, three albums in. Next day the press alleges students at two universities rigged the online poll.
years.xp: Steps and 5ive were among the acts they upset. Defenders pointed out that the band naturally appealed to students, that Campbell had attended one of the universities named, and that awards ought to reflect artistic merit rather than sales.

years.h: The band throws its own festival, the first Bowlie Weekender
years.p: Belle and Sebastian host it themselves, and bring the idea back in 2019 on a cruise ship.

yt: Legal Man, from Fold Your Hands Child
years.h: Top ten at last, and critics hear a band stalling
years.p: Fold Your Hands Child, You Walk Like a Peasant is the first UK top-ten album. Legal Man, co-written by Campbell, reaches No. 15 and gets the band on Top of the Pops.

years.h: Jack Black files them under sad bastards in High Fidelity
years.p: Jack Black's record-store clerk dismisses Belle and Sebastian this way in the film, while a clip of Seymour Stein plays in the scene.

years.h: The bassist who co-founded the band goes off to write novels
years.p: Stuart David quits to concentrate on Looper and books; his first novel, Nalda Said, came out in 1999. [[Bobby Kildea|02807e7c-66a4-4d8c-8abc-7b94d089bd85]] of V-Twin replaces him.

years.h: A Todd Solondz film gets a Belle and Sebastian soundtrack
years.p: The band spends much of the year touring and scoring Storytelling.

years.src: Wikipedia: Isobel Campbell · Wikipedia: Belle and Sebastian
years.h: Isobel Campbell walks out partway through a North American tour
years.p: She leaves the US and Canadian dates to go solo, and later makes three albums with [[Mark Lanegan|a9126556-f555-4920-9617-6e013f8228a7]], including the Mercury-nominated Ballad of the Broken Seas.
years.xp: She had already made records as The Gentle Waves in 1999 and 2000. The BBC Sessions album (2008) includes some of her last recordings with the band.

years.h: Four albums at Rough Trade
years.p: Belle and Sebastian leave Jeepster for a four-album deal with Rough Trade Records. Matador keeps releasing them in America.

eras.title: From Trevor Horn to the Hollywood Bowl
eras.text: A pop producer at the desk, a run of chart singles and 18,000 people in Los Angeles turned the shy band into a big one.

years.h: Aiming for the radio with Trevor Horn at the desk
years.p: Murdoch returns as main songwriter on Dear Catastrophe Waitress, produced by the man behind [[The Buggles|20278bbd-271a-4a1c-b6fd-43a13d43203d]] and [[Frankie Goes to Hollywood|c09c8263-40ef-4352-8031-e438b1ce68fc]]. It restores their indie credibility.

years.cap: The full band: Mick Cooke, Richard Colburn, Bobby Kildea, Chris Geddes, Stevie Jackson, Sarah Martin and Stuart Murdoch
years.h: Their highest UK chart placing yet, at No. 14
years.p: I'm a Cuckoo, a Thin Lizzy-flavoured single, brings Mercury Prize and Ivor Novello nominations.

years.h: War on Want takes members to Israel and the Palestinian territories
years.p: The April trip with the UK charity leads to The Eighth Station of the Cross Kebab House, later a B-side of Funny Little Frog.

yt: The Blues Are Still Blue video
years.h: The Life Pursuit reaches UK No. 8 and cracks the US chart
years.p: Produced by Tony Hoffer in California and first planned as a double album, it reaches No. 65 on the Billboard 200. Funny Little Frog debuts at No. 13 in the UK.

years.cap: Live at Summer Sundae, Leicester, August 2006
years.h: A sold-out Hollywood Bowl, with the LA Philharmonic
years.p: Eighteen thousand seats fill, and [[The Shins|6c8b9855-ba8b-48f9-ac1d-42167f7f7b18]] open.

eras.title: A long middle age, and a lost drummer
eras.text: After almost four years away from British stages, the band settled into festivals, a film, a trumpeter's exit and a drummer left behind in North Dakota.

years.cap: On stage at the Slottsfjell festival, Tonsberg, Norway, July 2010
years.h: Latitude gets the first UK show in almost four years
years.p: About 30,000 people at Henham Park in Suffolk hear two new songs, I Didn't See It Coming and I'm Not Living in the Real World.

years.cap: Live at the Wang Theatre, Boston, October 15, 2010
yt: I Want the World to Stop video
years.h: Norah Jones and Carey Mulligan sing on Write About Love
years.p: The eighth album reaches UK No. 8. [[Norah Jones|985c709c-7771-4de3-9024-7bda29ebe3f9]] sings on one song and the actor Carey Mulligan on the title track.

years.cap: Belle and Sebastian at the Sonorama festival, Spain, August 2013
years.h: Trumpeter Mick Cooke goes after fifteen years
years.p: He confirms in late 2013 that he's left the band on good terms.

years.h: Murdoch's first film as writer and director premieres at Sundance
years.p: He wrote and directed the musical God Help the Girl in 2012 and 2013.

years.h: Girls in Peacetime Want to Dance brings in a Teenage Fanclub bassist
years.p: Recorded in Atlanta, the ninth album is the first with touring bassist Dave McGowan of [[Teenage Fanclub|e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588]]. In June they play Glastonbury's Other Stage.

years.cap: Belle and Sebastian live on the 2017 tour
years.h: The band drives off without Richard Colburn at a North Dakota Walmart
years.p: On a US tour, Belle and Sebastian accidentally leave their drummer behind.

years.cap: On stage at TRNSMT, Glasgow Green
years.h: Dave McGowan, long on the road with them, becomes a member
years.p: The Teenage Fanclub bassist joins for good on November 3. Three How to Solve Our Human Problems EPs came out from December 2017 to February 2018.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates McGowan's touring with the band from 2012 to 2018; other accounts say 2011. His first album with the band was Girls in Peacetime Want to Dance in 2015.

years.cap: At the Royal Oak Music Theatre, Michigan, July 2019
years.h: A cruise ship hosts the band's 20th-anniversary festival
years.p: The Boaty Weekender revives the Bowlie idea on a Mediterranean cruise. The Days of the Bagnold Summer soundtrack follows.

eras.title: Two albums in eight months
eras.text: Twenty-six years after Tigermilk, Belle and Sebastian put out a new album, then surprised everyone with another.

years.h: Eleven albums in, A Bit of Previous
years.p: The eleventh studio album arrives in May 2022, 26 years after Tigermilk.

years.cap: Murdoch at the Palace Theatre, St. Paul, Minnesota
years.h: No warning, then Late Developers
years.p: The single I Don't Know What You See in Me arrives January 9, and the album four days later.
play: I Don't Know What You See in Me
